text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The central bank said it had proposed the Slovak part of the former Czechoslovak gold reserves, currently held in Prague, to be returned to Bratislava next week.
- President Michal Kovac on Wednesday officially appointed Jan Jasovsky as Minister of Transport, Post and Telecommunications.
- Banska Bystrica-based Banka Slovakia said it posted an after-tax profit of 3.8 million crowns in 1996.

- The opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL) said the National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, used shares of oil refiner Slovnaft from its portfolio as security for loans taken to help improve its liquidity.
- The SDL said the NPF's lingering liquidity problems will make it difficult to repay privatisation bonds, issued last year as a replacement for the voucher privatisation method.
- A special commission which will organise and supervise two forthcoming referenda -- on NATO membership and direct presidential elections -- holds its first meeting on Thursday.
- Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said EBRD officials had assured him the bank wanted to continue extending loans in Slovakia.
PRAVDA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said Slovakia may turn to the International Court of Justice if Prague and Bratislava fail to resolve the case.

SME - The official Economic Prognostic Institute says Slovakia's troubled foreign trade balance should be improved by more effective export production which could be boosted by larger foreign investment.
- The NPF is expected to decrease its stake in Banka Slovakia a.s. It is not known how large a stake in the bank the NPF holds.
- The current cold weather can seriously damage a large part of the agricultural production, mainly fruit trees. Experts expect a shortage of peaches and apricots on the domestic market this year.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Parliamentary committees are, at present, discussing the so-called revitalisation law, opposed by the opposition as creating unequal conditions in restructuring of troubled companies.
- The NBS said it would start issuing licences for mortgage banking soon.
